corrections.text: The article says The Register describes a per-core license while Ars Technica and TechTarget describe a figure that does not fall below the 128-core level, and that none of the cited reports says how the two descriptions relate. Ars Technica itself reports both: the per-core subscription license (attributed to The Register) and TD Synnex's $9,600-a-year listing for up to 128 cores. TechTarget quotes C4C Group's Nick Watson saying "Every estate below 128 cores pays for 128 [cores]", which points to a 128-core minimum. No cited report states the per-core rate or a minimum explicitly.

The article says The Register's "analysis section says the reception of Express may be mixed" in a paragraph about the Register's November 5 report on the EEA terms. That view appears only in the Register's November 4 vSphere Express report, where the correspondent writes that Express "will get a mixed reception"; the November 5 report has no analysis section.
